title: Comparing and Ordering Numbers to 100,000
seo_title: Grade 3 Comparing and Ordering Numbers to 100,000 Worksheets (TEKS 3.2D, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.2D compare and order whole numbers up to 100,000 and represent comparisons using the symbols >, <, or =
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.2D: compare numbers to 100,000 with >, < and =, find the greatest and least, order numbers, missing digits and word problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Compare from the left. The first place where the digits differ decides.
key_sub: > means greater than and < means less than. The open side faces the greater number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A number with more digits is greater: 10,000 > 9,999.
  • If the numbers have the same number of digits, compare from the left. The first place where the digits differ decides.
  • > means is greater than. < means is less than. The open side faces the greater number.
  • To order, find the least, then the next, and so on.

Examples

Example

Order 38,915; 38,519; 9,999 from least to greatest.

9,999 has 4 digits, so it is least.

38,915 and 38,519: the hundreds are 9 and 5.

5 < 9, so 38,519 comes next.

Answer: 9,999; 38,519; 38,915

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the ones digits firstStart at the left, with the greatest place.
Thinking the number with more 9s is greaterLook at the first place where the digits differ, not how many 9s there are.
Reading > and < backwardThe open mouth faces the greater number.

faq.a: Compare and order whole numbers up to 100,000 and show the comparison with >, < or =.

faq.q: How do you compare two 5-digit numbers?
faq.a: Line them up by place value and compare from the ten thousands place. The first place with different digits tells which number is greater.
The symbol opens toward the greater number: 52,000 > 25,000.

faq.q: What if the numbers have a different number of digits?
faq.a: The number with more digits is greater. Any 5-digit number is greater than any 4-digit number.
